text.en:
Ria ate a plate of idli. Farmers had grown the rice and urad. A mill ground them into flour and a shop sold it. A cook made the idli and a delivery boy brought it.
"So many people worked to make my breakfast," she said.

Economic activities are things people do to earn money or produce goods and services we need.
Primary activities take things from nature: farming, fishing, mining and cutting wood.
Secondary activities turn raw things into other things: factories make cloth, a mill turns wheat into flour, a carpenter makes a table.
Tertiary activities are services: teaching, healing, transport, banking, shopping and communication.
Long ago people exchanged goods directly (barter). Now we use money. Markets and shops bring producers and buyers together. We buy what we need and also what we want.
Economic activities are things we do to earn and to provide goods and services.
Primary activities take from nature, like farming, fishing and mining.
Secondary activities make new things, like a mill making flour.
Tertiary activities are services, like teaching, healing and transport.

problem.en: A farmer grows wheat, a mill makes flour and a shop sells it. Which activity is each?

text.en: Growing wheat takes from nature: primary.
The mill makes flour from wheat: secondary.
The shop sells to people: tertiary.

prompt.en: A friend says a teacher does not do any economic activity because she makes nothing. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: A teacher provides a service, which is a tertiary activity.
Services are an important part of the economy.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking only things you can touch count.

points.en: Primary: from nature. Secondary: making things. Tertiary: services.
Markets bring sellers and buyers together.
